The narrator continues, "Hadhrat Amr (RA) then left, the people scattered and Allaah removed the plague from them. When the opinion of Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) reached (Ameerul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA), he said "I swear by Allaah that he did not condemn it."[^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA) Concerning the Plague of Amwaas

Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates that when the plague struck Shaam, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) said, "This is a scourge that has come so flee from it to the mountains and ravines." When this statement reached Hadhrat Mu'aadh (RA), far from confirming it, he said, "Not at all! It is martyrdom, a mercy and the du'aa of your Nabi ﷺ." Hadhrat Abu Qilaabah narrates further, "While I knew that it was a form of martyrdom and a mercy, I did not know how it was the du'aa of Rasulullaah ﷺ until I was informed that while performing salaah one night, Rasulullaah ﷺ thrice made du'aa saying, 'Then let it be fever or a plague.' The following morning, one of his family members asked, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I overheard you making a du'aa last night.' 'You heard it?' Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. 'I certainly did,' came the reply. Rasulullaah ﷺ then explained, 'I asked my Rabb not to let my Ummah perish through drought and this du'aa was accepted. I then prayed to Allaah never to allow an enemy to overpower them and annihilate them (this was also granted). I also prayed to Him never to let my Ummah fragment into groups, waging wars against each other. This du'aa however was refused. It was then that I thrice said, 'Then let it be fever or a plague'."[^2]
Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA)'s Joy at the Plague

Hadhrat Urwa bin Zubayr (RA) reports that Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) and his family were unaffected by the plague of Amwaas when he prayed to Allaah saying, "O Allaah! Grant the family of Abu Ubaydah their share." When a sore erupted on his little finger, Hadhrat Abu Ubaydah (RA) started looking at (thinking that it was a sign of the plague) but he was assured that it meant nothing. He then said, "I wish that Allaah blesses it because when he blesses something little, it becomes a lot."[^3]
